caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the accuracy of various AI safety guard models in detecting harmful prompts under a few-shot learning setting, specifically for code attacks involving Python lists. The x-axis represents the number of few-shot examples, ranging from 0 to 5 in integer increments, with a linear scale. The y-axis shows accuracy, ranging from 50 to 95 in increments of 5, also on a linear scale. Six models are compared: OmniGuard (black solid line with circular markers), AegisGuard (P) (purple dashed line with circular markers), AegisGuard (D) (red solid line with circular markers), LlamaGuard 1 (green solid line with square markers), LlamaGuard 2 (orange solid line with square markers), and DuoGuard (dark purple dashed line with circular markers). Error bars are present for all lines, indicating the standard error of the mean across 50 random sets of few-shot examples. OmniGuard starts at approximately 50% accuracy with 0 few-shot examples and rises sharply to over 90% accuracy by 1 example, maintaining near-perfect accuracy (around 93%) at 5 examples. LlamaGuard 2 shows a gradual increase from about 85% to 90% accuracy. AegisGuard (P) begins at around 70% accuracy, peaks at approximately 78% at 1 example, then declines to about 53% at 5 examples. AegisGuard (D) starts at about 65%, dips slightly to around 55% at 1 example, and remains relatively flat around 55% thereafter. LlamaGuard 1 remains nearly constant at around 50% accuracy across all few-shot counts. DuoGuard starts at approximately 70% accuracy, drops to about 50% at 1 example, and stays around 50% for the remaining points.
